question.problem: Calculate the volume of a cylinder given that the circumference of the base is $14\pi \,\text{m}$ and the ratio of its height to its radius is $\frac{1}{49}.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the radius $r$ using the formula $C=2\pi r,$ where $C$ is the circumference, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}C & =2\pi r \\ 14\pi  & =2\pi r \\ r & =7\,\text{m}\end{aligned}
$$

To find the height $h$, we use the fact that the ratio of the height to the radius is $\frac{1}{49}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{h}{r} & =\frac{1}{49} \\ \frac{h}{7} & =\frac{1}{49} \\ h & =\frac{1}{7}\,\text{m}\end{aligned}
$$

The volume of a cylinder with radius $r$ and height $h$ is given by

$$
V=\pi {r}^{2}h.
$$

Substituting $r=7\,\text{m}$ and $h=\frac{1}{7}\,\text{m}$ into the formula, we get

$$
V=\pi \cdot {7}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{7}=7\pi \,{\text{m}}^{3}.
$$
